To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the BDNV Val66Met polymorphisn is associated with the dynamic functional connectivity patterns of pain modulatory system and that the resilient brain dynamics may be a vulnerability for chronic pain in women with PMD.
the BDNV Val66Met polymorphisms are associated with the functional dynamics of the PAG in PDM subjects.
the BDNV Val66Met polymorphisms contribute to the dynamic functional connectivity of pain modulatory brain networks in primary dysmenorhea.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of PDM, which may help to develop more personalized treatments for the disorder.
the BDNF-related genetic variations and the functional connectivity dynamics in pain modulatory systems during PDM.
the genetic and neural mechanisms that may underpin the pathogenesis of PDM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the BDNV Val66Met polymorphisms contribute towards the susceptibility of PDM and the genotype-dependent FC dynamics of the descending pain modulation system may be a potential biomarker of the disease.
the BDNV Val66Met polymorphisms may contribute towards the functional expression of pain modulatory pathways and, thus, the susceptibility of PDM.
the BDNV Val66Met polymorphisms are related to the dynamic functional connectivity of the PAG and its pain modulation in the context of primary dysmenorrheal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BDNV Val66Met polymorphic variation is a genetic determinant for pain modulation and the functional connectivity patterns of the PAG.
the BDNV Val66Met polymorphisms contribute to the individual variability in the functional connectivity dynamics and the pain susceptibility of PAG in PDM.
the BDNV Val66Met polymorphisms may be a potential biomarker for pain-related disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic predisposition and the pain experience may interact to modulate the functional dynamics of descending pain modulatory pathways.

the BDNV Val66Met genotype is a potential biomarker of the pain modulation in women with PMD, and that the PAG-seeded resting-state fMRI may be used to predict the pain modulation in the context of the BDNV polymorphism.
PAG FC dynamics may be used as an imaging marker of PDM and that the BDNV Val66Met polymorphic variation is associated with the FC dynamics of the descending pain pathways in PDM subjects.
